summary:
The team developed EXTENDS-CARE, an intelligent biomedical telemetry and clinical decision-support platform designed for astronauts on long-duration spaceflight missions. As crews venture toward the Moon and Mars, one-way communication delays of up to 22 minutes make real-time reliance on Earth-based flight surgeons impossible, requiring non-medical crew members to manage complex health emergencies autonomously.

EXTENDS-CARE addresses this challenge by integrating real-time physiological, behavioral, and environmental telemetry—including heart rate, SpO2, core temperature, blood pressure, intracranial/intraocular pressure (SANS), sleep debt, salivary cortisol, bone mineral density, cabin gases (CO2/O2/CO), and radiation dosimetry—into an intuitive, responsive web interface. The platform features an interactive 7-subsystem color-coded anatomical scanner powered by a 3-layer pessimistic Risk Engine that cross-references live wearable sensor streams against the official NASA LxC (Likelihood × Consequence) risk matrix and Design Reference Mission (DRM) timelines. When an anomaly is detected, the system triggers cascade alerts and delivers state-dependent, autonomous clinical countermeasures based on NASA-STD-3001 and Human Research Program (HRP) protocols.
details:
WHAT DOES EXTENDS-CARE DO AND HOW DOES IT WORK?

EXTENDS-CARE is a real-time crew health monitoring and autonomous clinical decision-support web application built for human spaceflight missions across Low Earth Orbit (LEO), Cis-Lunar/Gateway (LUNAR_ORBIT), Artemis Lunar Surface (LUNAR_SURFACE), and Deep Space/Mars (MARS) regimes.

The platform operates through a 3-Layer Pessimistic Risk Engine that evaluates each astronaut's health in real time:

1. Layer 1 — Systemic Vital Signs & Pessimistic Cascade: Continuously monitors core vital signs (Heart Rate, Blood Oxygen SpO2, Core Body Temperature, and HRV/Cortisol Stress Index). If a primary vital sign breaches nominal corridors into Caution or Critical thresholds, a systemic cascade alert automatically propagates across all anatomical subsystems to prioritize immediate clinical stabilization.

2. Layer 2 — NASA LxC Temporal Risk Matrix: Dynamically maps 16 official NASA Human Research Program (HRP) risks across 7 anatomical regions based on the active mission's Design Reference Mission (DRM) category and Mission Elapsed Time (MET). It calculates operational and long-term health severity using Likelihood × Consequence (LxC) scores and NASA risk dispositions.

3. Layer 3 — Subsystem-Specific Wearable & Habitat Sensors: Evaluates 5 specialized telemetry suites:

• Ocular Pressure (SANS): Intraocular pressure (IOP), intracranial pressure (ICP), translaminar gradient ratio, and optic nerve deformation.

• Neurological: Cumulative sleep debt, sleep efficiency, blink rate, and pupil dilation.

• Behavioral: Salivary cortisol, galvanic skin response (GSR), and heart rate variability (HRV).

• Cardiopulmonary: Systolic/diastolic blood pressure, respiratory rate, and personal breathable O2 percentage.

• Bone Density & Immune: Bone Mineral Density (BMD), monthly BMD degradation rate, bone volume fraction, Collagen Type IV, and plasma fibronectin.

• Environment: Daily radiation rate (mSv/day), cumulative career dose (against the 600 mSv limit), cabin CO2 (ppm/mmHg), carbon monoxide (CO), and total cabin pressure.

All data is visualized through a main focused view (featuring an interactive 7-region SVG anatomical scanner and live vital signs panel), a secondary multi-crew telemetry grid for rapid switching between astronauts, a mission orbital KPI tracker, and a dedicated subsystem detail view (system-details) that generates state-dependent operational countermeasures.

KEY BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

• Autonomous Medical Triage Under Communication Delays: With up to 22-minute one-way communication blackouts on Mars missions, crews cannot wait for Mission Control (MCC) to diagnose acute events. EXTENDS-CARE translates raw multi-sensor telemetry into clear visual statuses (Nominal, Caution, Sensor Alert, Critical) and actionable, step-by-step countermeasures that non-physician astronauts can execute immediately.

• Prevention of Compound Stressor Synergies: In spaceflight, isolated mild stressors (such as <6 hours of sleep combined with elevated cabin CO2 ~2,500 ppm and high workload) compound exponentially into critical operational errors. Our engine detects multi-system deviations early and prescribes targeted interventions (e.g., SSLA blue-light protocols, LBNP fluid-shift reversal, ARED resistive loading, or Storm Shelter evacuation during Solar Particle Events).

• Earth & Space Impact: Beyond supporting Artemis and Mars exploration, EXTENDS-CARE's modular architecture is directly adaptable to Isolated, Confined, and Extreme (ICE) terrestrial environments, such as polar research stations, submarine crews, offshore platforms, and remote rural telemedicine.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE MODELS & SOFTWARE USED

• Frontend Architecture: HTML5 (modularized via asynchronous DOM injection with loader.js), responsive CSS3 structured into 6 domain-specific stylesheets (base.css, navbar.css, scanner.css, crew.css, mission.css, detail.css), and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+ custom event-driven state management via window.AppState).

• Backend & Cloud Infrastructure: Google Firebase Realtime Database (REST API multi-path PATCH/PUT synchronization) and Firebase Hosting for globally distributed, low-latency deployment.

• Telemetry Simulation Engine: Python 3 scripts (using the requests library) and an interactive web-based Simulation & CRUD Control Console that generate realistic physiological and orbital data streams every 10 seconds.

• Modeled Spaceflight Hardware & Instruments: Telemetry ranges and sensor structures are modeled after real ISS/agency hardware, including the CSA Bio-Monitor Smart Shirt (Hexoskin), ESA Thermolab, NASA Personal CO2 Monitor (PCO2M), TDLAS, Major Constituent Analyzer (MCA), Air Quality Monitor (AQM), Crew Active Dosimeter (CAD), Radi-N2, and Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT).

• Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, Firebase CLI, Git, and Chrome DevTools.

HOW IS THE PROJECT CREATIVE?

Rather than treating medical telemetry as isolated numbers on a spreadsheet, EXTENDS-CARE unifies static aerospace risk matrices (NASA's LxC tables) with live wearable sensor streams inside an interactive anatomical twin. Clicking any crew card in the secondary grid seamlessly promotes that astronaut to the main scanner, while clicking any of the 7 body regions opens a clinical breakdown pairing real-time sensor readings with dynamic protocols tailored to the exact severity state.

FACTORS CONSIDERED BY THE TEAM

• NASA-STD-3001 & HRP Clinical Standards: All alarm thresholds and countermeasures were engineered around official space medicine models, including Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), bone resorption (1.0–1.7% monthly BMD loss), circadian desynchronization, decompression sickness (DCS), and the 600 mSv career radiation limit.

• Human-System Integration Architecture (HSIA) & Cognitive Ergonomics: During an in-flight emergency, astronauts suffer from cognitive overload and alarm fatigue. We designed a clean, high-contrast light clinical interface with strict color-coding and responsive layouts so the dashboard remains legible across spacecraft workstations, tablets, and mobile devices.
